title: Selection or drift? Aggression gene vs a neutral marker under scarcity
question: Experiment D found a higher aggression gene under scarcity but no change in attack behaviour, and scarce worlds ran through ~2x more generations. Does the aggression gene rise beyond a neutral marker that is inherited and mutated identically but has no effect?
background: A neutral marker is the standard control for genetic drift: it shares the aggression gene's inheritance, mutation and clipping but is never read by behaviour. Selection on aggression predicts aggression > marker. Pure drift predicts no systematic difference.

hypotheses.statement: Under scarcity the aggression gene exceeds the neutral marker (selection)
The aggression-minus-marker excess is larger under scarcity than abundance
The neutral marker itself is higher under scarcity (drift/clipping with more generations)
